title: OpenAPI embedded example value under a credential-named header parameter
summary: The twin of the reference-only example case: the same X-Api-Key header parameter, but the example is resolved into an embedded value holding an opaque 40-character literal with no placeholder marking and no provider-documented format. No fixture is authored.
rationale: Once the pointer is resolved the span is a literal, and the specification has nothing to say about whether it is a placeholder or a private value: it says examples show usage, may be returned by mock servers, represent the final serialized form of the data and override schema examples. A literal in an example can be a documented placeholder (covered by the documentation-placeholder scenario), a value whose own grammar establishes a credential regardless of this wrapper (carried by the family's own cases), or an opaque string with neither signal. Only the third is this case, and the sources do not settle it. A rejected reading is that a header parameter named Authorization is ignored by the specification and therefore its example is not sensitive: the specification ignores the parameter definition, not the bytes the document holds.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved. The sources read describe what an example is for (usage demonstration, mock responses, the final serialized form) and that a header parameter named Authorization is ignored; none says whether an embedded example value is a placeholder or a real value, and none classifies an opaque literal. Candidate outcomes: not flagged when the document marks the value as a placeholder; flagged when the value's grammar establishes a credential; and for the unmarked opaque literal either, depending on a maintainer decision (project-policy with a non-author reviewer) or a statement by the API's provider. Planned fixture, not built: the reference case's fragment with a components example whose value is a 40-character string built from a repeated authored word run and the letters of an obviously fake marker, wrapped under X-Api-Key. Generated request samples that insert this value into a curl or SDK snippet are a tool behavior the sources do not describe; any scoring of them waits for the credential-eval contract (#150).

sources.supports: The examples (plural) fields in the Parameter and Media Type Objects show example values formatted as they would appear serialized; because they represent the final serialized form of the data, they override any example in the corresponding Schema Object.
If in is header and the name field is Accept, Content-Type or Authorization, the parameter definition shall be ignored.
Example objects can be used by mock servers as return values.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. The OpenAPI Specification is a standard with no issuing provider; it is cited only for its own text, never for what any provider issues. Reference resolution, example generation, request-sample generation and masking are tool behaviors owned downstream (credential-eval, #150); no scanner or adapter capability is assumed.
